skill.name: blazor
skill.description: Blazor WebAssembly frontend for VanDaemon running on .NET 10. Components live in `src/Frontend/VanDaemon.Web/Pages/`. Uses MudBlazor for Material Design UI and SignalR for real-time updates from the API.

generated_query: I need to add a real-time monitoring dashboard for tank levels in our VanDaemon system. Currently, I have a basic page that shows all tanks, but I want to extend it so that when a tank level drops below 20%, a warning card appears at the top with a Mudthe required capability alert, and the alert auto-dismisses when the level goes back above 20%. The data comes from a SignalR hub that sends `TankLevelUpdated` events. Also, I need the page to filter tanks by name using a MudTextField with two-way binding. Can you write the Razor component for this page, including the SignalR subscription and the conditional rendering for the low-level alert? The component should live in `src/Frontend/VanDaemon.Web/Pages/`.

edit_instructions.rationale: Deleting the level update prevents the UI from reflecting real-time tank level changes, so the low-level alert cannot auto-dismiss when the level rises above 20%.
Deleting the two-way binding example removes guidance for implementing the MudTextField filter with @bind, a key requirement in the query.

Replaces the real-time SignalR subscription with periodic HTTP polling, which cannot receive immediate TankLevelUpdated events and thus fails the user's requirement for real-time alerts that auto-dismiss.
Changes the SignalR event name, so the component will never subscribe to the actual 'TankLevelUpdated' events the user's system sends.
Inserts a low-level warning card but without any auto-dismiss logic, failing the user's requirement that alerts disappear when levels rise above 20%.

Adds a MudTextField binding in the UI (via `@bind-Value="_filterText"`) and a filter property, but the `@bind-Value` line is omitted from the Razor template, so filtering never actually works despite the two-way binding being mentioned.
